item.title: [github_trending] DietrichGebert/ponytail
item.description: Ponytail is an open-source project that steers AI agents toward the mindset of the laziest senior dev: write as little as possible, because the best code is the code you never wrote. It says it works with 20 agents, is MIT-licensed, and ships an npm package. A useful experiment for teams tired of agents overengineering simple tasks.

item.title: [producthunt] Kilo Code for JetBrains
item.description: Kilo Code for JetBrains is a fully native, open-source coding agent built specifically for JetBrains IDEs, rather than a web-based or external plugin tool. Because it runs inside the IDE, developers can get AI-agent assistance while staying in the editor they already use. It is aimed at JetBrains users who want the flexibility of an open-source coding agent in their existing toolchain.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: The author, after switching from Cursor to Codex for over half a month, says Cursor first showed him AI coding's impact, but Codex makes him feel AI is not merely a coding assistant—it behaves like a true super agent and is closer to the next stage. Developers deciding whether to migrate from Cursor to Codex will find this firsthand perspective useful.

item.title: [infoq] Fable 5.1 正式发布：性能翻倍、Agent成本下降45%，Anthropic 把顶级模型送进真实世界
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 as two safety tiers of the same model: Fable is generally available, while Mythos is restricted to vetted institutions. Fable 5.1 scores about twice as high as its predecessor on an agentic-science benchmark and can cut agent-call costs by up to 45%; risky requests may be blocked or routed to a weaker model. The approach decouples raw capability from who can use it in production.

item.title: [v2ex] [问与答] R2S 跑 OpenClash 老死机，想换机， R4S / R5S / R76S / N100 怎么选？
item.description: The author's R2S running OpenClash keeps crashing with odd bugs, and AnyTLS misbehaves after prolonged use, so he plans a replacement. Options he's weighing include the R4S/R5S for their abundant firmware, the cheaper R76S whose firmware ecosystem looks sparse, and the J4125/N100 which he fears is overkill for pure internet browsing; he asks which suits this daily-use case.

item.description: Cloudflare has open-sourced Cloudflare OS, an enterprise AI platform where each document, dashboard or data view runs in an isolated V8 sandbox called a Gadget, giving users a personal, modifiable copy. The isolation is meant to let non-technical users safely build custom software, with a capability-driven model enforcing enterprise policy. The project originated from internal incidents where employees deployed unapproved GenAI workflows with excessive permissions and API-token access.

item.title: [hackernews] .name Termination
item.description: Neil Fraser reports that Verisign proposed deleting the entire third-level .name hierarchy in April 2026, and ICANN approved it on July 28. His neil.fraser.name has hosted his website, email and an API server for nearly 25 years, and he also registered one for his daughter; he learned about the change only from his registrar's email. The post explains why third-level domains are more fragile than second-level ones.

item.title: [github_trending] debpalash/VoiceStudio
item.description: VoiceStudio, formerly OmniVoice-Studio, is an open-source and fully local alternative to ElevenLabs that bundles voice cloning, video dubbing, dictation, transcription, and audiobook creation with a claimed 646-language catalogue. It is built on 16 TTS and 11 ASR engines, requires no account or API key for local runs, and supports macOS, Windows, Linux, and Docker. Developers who want full control over voice workloads and data privacy are the target audience.

item.title: [infoq] 倒计时21天！GOAI进入决赛月，120强全力冲刺
item.description: The World AI Open Source Competition (GOAI) will hold its Hangzhou finals on Sept 22–24, running alongside the Yunqi Conference and Digital Trade Expo, with a 5-million-RMB total prize pool. About 120 teams advanced from 2,999 initial entries. The 100 teams across three main tracks must submit round-two materials by 18:00 on Sept 3 to fight for 50 finals slots, while the 20 embodied-future teams are already in the finals doing real-hardware debugging.

The GitHub repo now carries a TimesFM 3.0 PyTorch checkpoint, plus integrations with BigQuery ML, Google Sheets, and Vertex Model Garden. By turning conventional motion-design workflows into conversational commands, it lowers the barrier to quickly producing dynamic assets for editors and marketers. The tool is pitched as a faster option for teams without deep editing expertise.

item.title: [github_trending] mattpocock/skills
item.description: Matt Pocock open-sourced his personal AI agent skills in mattpocock/skills, taken from his own .agents directory and used for real engineering, not vibe coding. Unlike frameworks like GSD, BMAD, or Spec-Kit that own the whole process, these skills are deliberately small, adaptable, composable, and model-agnostic, giving developers more control. He encourages hacking on them and making them your own.

item.title: [infoq] Nuxt 4.5：实验性 SSR 流式传输、Vite 8 以及基于 Rsbuild 的 Rspack 构建器
item.description: Nuxt 4.5, billed by the team as a major release, moves the build toolchain to Vite 8, switches the Rspack 2 builder to an Rsbuild-based setup, and adds experimental SSR streaming, a stable error-code scheme, and the useLayout composable. Streaming sends an HTML shell immediately to cut TTFB, though it doesn't reduce the server-side processing time shown at 2.5 seconds and is disabled for crawlers. Use nuxt upgrade --dedupe when upgrading because unhead v3 introduces breaking changes.

item.title: [github_trending] blader/humanizer
item.description: Humanizer is a Markdown-based agent skill that rewrites AI-sounding text to read naturally without changing its meaning. It applies 35 patterns from Wikipedia's 'Signs of AI writing' (maintained by WikiProject AI Cleanup), then checks the draft against those patterns and the original claims, never inventing names, dates, or quotes. Built as plain Markdown, it works with any agent supporting skills and can follow a writing sample for style.

item.title: [infoq] Diagrid Catalyst 2.0 发布，为 AI 智能体新增持久化、可验证的执行能力
item.description: On July 28, 2026, Diagrid shipped Catalyst 2.0, adding durable, verifiable execution for AI agents built with LangGraph, Google ADK, Dapr Agents, and other frameworks. Ten framework integrations are supported; model and tool calls are recorded as workflow activities so interrupted runs resume without redoing completed calls. The verification layer, inherited from Dapr 1.18, hashes and signs workflow history for validation outside the originating app — signing is off by default and requires mTLS.
